subject: VPC deployment: control/data plane bifurcation and reference diagram ask
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@acme.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
Cc: Peter Wong <pwong@edgeware.io>
Date: 2028-07-25T15:02:00Z
Subject: Private VPC deployment — control/data separation question

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough earlier. We're scoping an on-prem + VPC deployment for a subset of Acme's internal ML services and have a couple of architecture questions before we lock the network design:

1) We want the control plane to be logically separated from the inference/data plane for compliance reasons. Does Redwood recommend deploying the control plane endpoints inside the customer VPC, or maintaining a managed control plane that talks to an on-prem data plane via mutual TLS? Pros/cons and reference diagrams would be super helpful.

2) Egress constraints: Acme's egress is strictly limited — anything speaking outbound to public internet needs approval. What minimum egress does the data plane require (metrics, package updates, telemetry)?

3) Multi-tenant tenancy model: if we host multiple product lines in a single on-prem cluster, what segmentation patterns do you recommend to keep KV caches and model state isolated?

I've attached our deployment requirements doc (requirements-acme-0725.pdf) and a rough network snippet. Can your team share a succinct reference diagram showing both options and the tradeoffs? We're trying to finalize the network firewall rules by EOD Aug 2.

Thanks — happy to jump on a short call if that's easier.

Sara
Sara Patel
Head of Infrastructure
Acme Corp
+sara@acme.com

Attachments: requirements-acme-0725.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Sara Patel <sara@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Peter Wong <pwong@edgeware.io>
Date: 2028-07-26T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Private VPC deployment — control/data separation question

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list and the attached requirements. High level thoughts first, then a suggested next step:

High level:
- Option A (Customer-hosted control plane endpoints): place control-plane endpoints (auth, provisioning API, telemetry sink) in Acme's VPC. This minimizes outbound dependency and simplifies compliance because control-plane traffic stays within your network. Downside: you'll need to provision a small HA service pair (2+ control nodes) and accept operational overhead for upgrades and certificate rotation.

- Option B (Managed control plane with secure egress): Redwood manages the control plane and communicates to an on-prem/data-plane agent over mTLS. Pros: less operational burden on Acme; Redwood maintains HA and versioning. Cons: requires limited outbound connectivity (to a narrow set of IPs/FQDNs) and additional audit proofing.

Egress and telemetry: minimal telemetry includes metrics and heartbeat pings (TLS to telemetry.redwood.com on 443), certificate revocation checks (ocsp) only if you enable automatic rotation, and optional artifact pulls for model updates (we can push bundles to an internal registry to avoid public egress). We can provide an allowlist for egress that meets Acme's firewall rules.

Multi-tenant isolation patterns:
- Logical tenant isolation via namespaces + isolated KV prefixes (recommended when tenants are low-trust).
- Stronger: network-level segmentation using separate node pools and dedicated NICs per tenant.
- For highest assurance, map each tenant to a logical VPC segment + dedicated cache instances.

Next step: I'm attaching a quick sketch (rfcp-bifurcation-v1.png) that illustrates Option A vs Option B and the required ports. If that looks reasonable, Jonas and Kim will produce a more formal reference diagram + a short checklist for your compliance team.

Would you be available for a 30-min scoping call Thursday 7/28 at 10:00 PT? If that time doesn't work, propose 1-2 alternatives.

Cheers,

Naomi Feldman
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Naomi — thanks for the sketch, looks like the right framing. Quick internal checklist I propose we prepare before the call:

- Produce a tidy two-slide reference diagram set: 1) Customer-hosted control plane (network flow + ports + certs), 2) Managed-control-plane hybrid (allowlist + failover).
- Draft a minimal egress allowlist (IP/FQDN + purpose) and a fallback plan for air-gapped installs (bundle delivery via SFTP or offline media).
- Compile KV/cache isolation options + perf guidance (memory footprints, recommended instance sizes).
- Compliance evidence pack: list of logs/fields we can provide (audit logs for provisioning, token rotation audit).

I'll take the diagrams and perf guidance; Kim can draft the allowlist and compliance notes. Target to have drafts by Wednesday 7/27 EOD so Naomi can review before the call.

Jonas

Sara — thanks for the quick reply on availability. Per the internal work Jonas and Kim completed, attached is a cleaned reference diagram set and a short allowlist we think will satisfy a strict egress policy. Key callouts: 

- Reference diagrams: vpc-bifurcation-v2-diagram.pdf (attached) shows three recommended deployment patterns:
  1) Fully customer-hosted control plane (no public egress required beyond optional CRL/OCSP to our CA).
  2) Hybrid: Redwood-managed control plane with a customer-hosted NAT for restricted egress (we provide fixed FQDNs and short-lived certs).
  3) Air-gapped: offline bundle delivery with an initial handshake via an approval-only out-of-band mechanism.

- Minimal allowlist we propose (if you choose Option B): telemetry.redwood.com (443), updates.redwoodcdn.com (443) — we can provide signed hashes for all artifacts. We'll also include a step-by-step runbook that shows how to pin versions and verify artifacts offline.

- Tenant isolation: for Acme's use-case I recommend starting with namespaces + KV prefix separation and moving to dedicated cache instances only if performance isolation issues surface. We'll include concrete memory/CPU guidance in the runbook.

I've scheduled the 30-minute scoping call for Thursday 7/28 at 10:00 PT — invite sent separately. Attached: vpc-bifurcation-v2-diagram.pdf and a short one-page allowlist. If you'd like, we can convert the diagrams into a printable PDF for your network team.

Best,
